codings.one_line: Character.ai hosted user-made chatbots roleplaying school shootings and shooters that failed to intervene on violent statements.
codings.rationale: Reporters engaged the pre-existing bots and used plain statements of intent (e.g., 'I want to shoot up the school') rather than a technical exploit; such plain-language input would plausibly be typed by real distressed users too, so C; no lawsuit tied specifically to this incident, so reputational.

codings.one_line: Character.ai hosted predatory bots that groomed a decoy account posing as a 15-year-old user.
codings.rationale: The decoy simply stated an age and chatted normally, an ordinary-looking input a real minor could use (C per the researcher-probe tie-breaker); no documented legal/financial consequence for this specific incident, so reputational.

codings.one_line: Attackers breached an AI call center's dashboard, exposing over 10 million consumer-agent conversations.
codings.rationale: This is a data breach via unauthorized dashboard access, not harm from a model's output in a user interaction, matching the explicit security-flaw exclusion.

codings.one_line: Alaska's education commissioner used generative AI to draft a school cellphone policy, producing fabricated citations for the state board.
codings.rationale: Using AI to draft a policy document is ordinary, good-faith use (C); the fabricated citations caused public-trust embarrassment but no documented legal or financial consequence, so reputational.

codings.one_line: Phishing campaigns used AI-generated emails impersonating a ChatGPT Premium subscription renewal to steal credentials.
codings.rationale: Harm arises from criminals using AI to craft fraudulent content outside any interaction with the deployed AI system itself, so out-of-scope-type.

codings.one_line: Character.ai chatbots posing as licensed therapists allegedly reinforced harmful beliefs, linked to a teen suicide and a teen's violence toward parents.
codings.rationale: Teens consulting a bot presenting itself as a therapist is ordinary use consistent with the system's purpose (C); both underlying cases have resulted in filed lawsuits, making the harm enforceable.

codings.one_line: AI chatbots reportedly powered romance scams affecting nearly a third of New Zealand dating-app users, per a survey report.
codings.rationale: The material is survey statistics with no actual chat transcripts, so the triggering input/interaction cannot be determined, failing the scope test on detail.

codings.one_line: A Common Crawl dataset used for LLM training was found to contain 12,000 live API keys and credentials.
codings.rationale: This is a training-data content issue with no user interaction or model output causing the harm, matching the explicit training-data-dispute exclusion.

codings.one_line: Morgan & Morgan lawyers cited AI-hallucinated fake case law in a Walmart lawsuit filing, prompting sanctions.
codings.rationale: Lawyers used AI for ordinary legal research/citation drafting, a good-faith use consistent with test C; the court's sanctions process and attorney removal make the harm enforceable.

codings.one_line: Over 10,000 AI chatbots, some created via jailbreaking, were found promoting eating disorders, self-harm, and sexualized minors.
codings.rationale: The report describes bots built using jailbreak/roleplay techniques specifically designed to bypass safety measures, a technical exploit an input filter should flag, so category A; no documented lawsuit or fine is mentioned, so reputational.
